sentences.text: The appellant/Insurance Company has preferred this Appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'the Act, 1988') calling in question the legality, validity and correctness of the award dated 16.5.2018 passed by the Upper Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bemetara (for short 'the Claims Tribunal') in Claim Case No.72/2016 by which liability to pay compensation of Rs.9,77,200/- has been fastened on the Insurance Company.

entities.text: Upper Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bemetara
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Miss Prerna Agrawal, learned counsel for the appellant would submit that from perusal of the document (Ex.-D/3) it is quite vivid that the offending vehicle did not have fitness certificate on the date of the accident and, therefore, the Insurance Company is not liable in view of the provisions contained under Section 56 of the Act,
1988.
She also submits that the interest awarded by the Claims Tribunal is also on the higher side, which may be reduced to 6%.
3. On the other hand, Mr. Amit Kumar Sahu, learned counsel for the respondent/claimant would support the impugned award.
4. I have heard learned counsel for the parties, considered their rival submissions made herein-above and went through the records with utmost circumspection.

5. Though vide Ex.-D/3, officer of the Insurance Company has proved the fact that on 5.3.2015, the offending vehicle did not have fitness certificate, but vide Ex.-D/1,
which is a document filed and proved by the Insurance Company, validity of the fitness was up to 30 th December, 2017, which has been accepted by the Claims Tribunal, in which I do not find any illegality or perversity warranting interference.
6. So far as interest is concerned, the Claims Tribunal has awarded interest @ 9%
from the date of presentation of claim petition.

However, considering the entire facts situation of the case, rate of interest is reduced to 7% instead of 9%.
7.
The impugned award is modified to the extent indicated above and the Appeal is accordingly disposed of.

Sd/-
(Sanjay K. Agrawal) Judge Barve United India Insurance Company Limited vs Smt. Ramla Bai on 30 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90173699/
